questions: Did the bulging appearance of your eyes develop suddenly, over days or weeks?
Has the bulging been progressively worsening?
Is one eye more prominent than the other?
Do you have any loss or blurring of vision?
Do you have pain in or behind either eye?
Does moving your eyes cause pain?
Have your eyes become unusually red, swollen, or sensitive to light?
Have you had difficulty closing your eyelids completely?
Have you ever been diagnosed with thyroid disease?
Have you recently had weight loss, tremor, excessive sweating, or a racing heartbeat?
Have you had an injury, surgery, or infection around either eye recently?
Do you have severe headache, vomiting, weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking?
Have you had a similar episode in the past?
orders: Visual acuity, pupillary responses, color vision, and intraocular pressure examination
Hertel exophthalmometry and assessment for globe displacement
Ocular motility examination with cover–uncover and prism testing
Slit-lamp examination and dilated fundus examination
Assessment of eyelid laxity and attempt at gentle eyelid closure with globe repositioning
Thyroid-stimulating hormone, free T4, free T3, and TSH-receptor antibody levels
Contrast-enhanced MRI of the orbits and brain
results: 1. Visual acuity, pupillary responses, color vision, and intraocular pressure examination
pupil size and light reaction: equal and reactive
2. Hertel exophthalmometry and assessment for globe displacement
3. Ocular motility examination with cover–uncover and prism testing
skew deviation / alternating cover test: no vertical misalignment
4. Slit-lamp examination and dilated fundus examination
5. Assessment of eyelid laxity and attempt at gentle eyelid closure with globe repositioning
6. Thyroid-stimulating hormone, free T4, free T3, and TSH-receptor antibody levels
7. Contrast-enhanced MRI of the orbits and brain
MRI brain with gadolinium: bilateral dorsomedial pontine and left thalamic infarction
MRI sella and orbits: normal - no parasellar or suprasellar mass
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Wall-eyed bilateral internuclear ophthalmoplegia (WEBINO syndrome) caused by bilateral medial longitudinal fasciculus infarction from bilateral dorsomedial pontine ischemic stroke

ALTERNATIVE 1: Bilateral pontine infarction causing bilateral horizontal gaze disorder with exotropia

ALTERNATIVE 2: Ocular bobbing or other saccadic eye-movement disorder secondary to pontine infarction

ALTERNATIVE 3: Bilateral sixth cranial nerve palsy due to pontine ischemia
